correctness.rationale: For m,q≥2 and λ∈(0,1), τ∈(0,1], the Markov first-step equation on an unpinned vertex in a q-clique with s pinned and hub potential x is y_s(x)=λ(x+s)/(q−λ(q−s−1)). With pinned hub, sharp per-clique threshold b_s=y_s(1) yields minimum 1+mr, b_{r−1}<τ≤b_r. If hub is free, all cliques still need at least r pinned; exactly mr sources give uniform hub support b_{r−1}<τ and fail. At mr+1, exactly one clique has r+1, others r, and exact hub fixed-point x=X from rational linear response. Its minimum peripheral potential θ=y_r(X) satisfies b_{r−1}<θ<b_r, giving every hub-free optimum when τ≤θ and exactly the binomial count. The r=q and τ=1 boundary yields the whole graph uniquely. Independent exact-rational adjacency-first-step exhaustive enumeration of 148 tested (graph,λ,τ) cases and all nonempty source subsets corroborated both counts; arbitrary graph sizes and real thresholds follow from proof.
residual_risks: The strict interior threshold requires q≥2, m≥2, 0<λ<1 and graph symmetry; heterogeneous cliques are not covered.
Finite exact rational enumeration was independent of the symbolic block formula but tests only selected small parameters.

value.rationale: The originating discounted-hitting domination problem makes source-location optimization mathematically natural. Clique windmills give a motivated symmetric family bridging stars and non-tree block graphs, and this theorem calculates not just optimum cardinality but every optimum and an internal rational phase transition where many hub-free optimum sets vanish without any cardinality change. This classification is a complete meaningful extremizer problem for all real λ,τ rather than one numerical example.
residual_risks: The result is for homogeneous simple walks and equal clique sizes, not a general network-target algorithm.
